packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-10 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind; no outside source consulted, no identification attempted)

Exposure note: none. Only the images and PROMPT.md of this packet were read.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 (overview): inside of a front board of a very small volume. A strip of parchment
  manuscript is pasted on the board as a pastedown, upright; its left edge is cut (2-4 letters
  lost at the start of every line) and its right edge is whole. 22 lines visible, single column
  as preserved (narrow; may be one column of a larger page - cannot tell). Small gothic bookhand
  (textualis), black-brown ink; red strokes on capitals/paragraph breaks and red strike-throughs
  / underlines on a few words (lines 16, 19, 21, 22). Pencil "2248" above the text and a paper
  shelf-label "2248." pasted over the right part of the board. A clasp/tab at the left edge.
- image-004 (second overview): the facing first leaf. Right part: one column of the same or a
  very similar hand, 22 lines, right ends of lines cut by the edge of the leaf/crop (1-4 letters
  lost). Above line 1 a faint, rubbed line in smaller script that looks like a heading
  ("Renouat(ur)? ho(mo)? quot? modis"??) under still fainter larger erased writing. Left part of
  the leaf: blank margin with "Fra:" (later hand), pencil "2248", a small cursive marginal note
  of c. 7 short lines beside lines 5-9, another 2-line faint note lower, a rectangular frame
  drawn in ink with faded writing inside ("7... P..."?), and at the foot a small note
  "f. 49 ..."?. A pencilled "1"/"2" at upper right.
- Scriptural book names with chapter numerals occur in the text and are touched in red
  (e.g. "Iere. xxiiii", "Num. xi", "osee. xi", "ad tit. iii"); these are citation tags inside
  continuous prose, not headings. No enlarged initials, no interlinear gloss seen.
- Tentative interpretation: continuous moral/exegetical prose built from chains of scriptural
  quotations with short comments. Whether pastedown and first leaf are the same text is not
  determinable from the images (hands look alike).

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Read: all 22 lines of the pastedown (image-002 lines 1-11, image-003 lines for 9-22; the crops
overlap on lines 9-11) and all 22 lines of the right-hand column (image-005 lines 1-12,
image-006 lines 10-22; overlap on lines 10-12). Unread: the small cursive marginalia and the
framed note (too faint), the erased heading area, the next leaves visible only as an edge.

3. TRANSCRIPTION
(Line numbers = text lines counted from the top of the named image. "[..]" at line start = letters
lost at the cut left edge; I have not supplied them.)

A. Pastedown strip
image-002 L1:  [..]at? d(eu)s? . [illegible abbrev., "ap"/"eph"?] . xx. gen(er)at(i)o? medulla q(ue)?
image-002 L2:  [..]ui nos patiat(ur). et Iere. xxiiii. vos
image-002 L3:  [..]tis michi honus p(ro)iciam quippe
image-002 L4:  [..]os et c. Num. xi. Nu(m)quid ego con-
image-002 L5:  [..]i o(mn)em multitudinem hanc aut ge-
image-002 L6:  [..] ut? dicas michi porta eos sic(ut)
image-002 L7:  [..]rtare solet mat(er)? p(ar)uulu(m). ut
image-002 L8:  [..] eti(am)? sordes illor(um) excipias sic(ut) nut(ri)x
image-002 L9:  [..] mat(er) infantis q(ue) et pueri sic(ut)?         (= image-003 L1)
image-002 L10: [..]uent(ur)? inq(ui)nant(ur) sordib(us) et miserat(ur)?  (= image-003 L2)
image-002 L11: [..] tedio afficiunt(ur) fletib(us). osee. xi.       (= image-003 L3)
image-003 L4:  [..]o nut(ri)cius effrahym portans eos
image-003 L5:  [..] c. It(em)? est homo grauis humoris?
image-003 L6:  [..] xxii. harenam et salem et
image-003 L7:  [..]assam ferri. facilius est ferre
image-003 L8:  [..]am ho(m)i(n)em inprudente(m) et fa-     ["inprudentem" has a red stroke through/under it]
image-003 L9:  [..]m et impiu(m) talis bene co(m)parat(ur)?   [last word partly covered by red blot]
image-003 L10: [..]rene quia inutilis. sali quia
image-003 L11: [..]aciabilis. semp(er) .n. sitit p(ro)u(er)?.   [last word struck through in red]
image-003 L12: [..] desidia occid(un)t? pigru(m). ferro
image-003 L13: [..]a indomabil(is). masse quia inpor-     [red smear over "indomabilis"]
image-003 L14: [..]il(is). act(uum). xxii?. tolle? ...  .n. e?.    [bottom line, partly cut and smeared]

B. First leaf, right-hand column (line ends cut at right)
image-005 L0:  [faint heading above the column, smaller script] Renouat(ur)? ho(mo)? quot? modis?   (very doubtful)
image-005 L1:  ih(esu)m xp̄m qui reformauit corp(us) hu[..]
image-005 L2:  litatis n(ost)re et c. In p(ri)mo aduent[..]
image-005 L3:  venit d(eu)s animas reformare. et s[..]
image-005 L4:  reformatur homo p(er) bap(tis)m(um) ut de
image-005 L5:  vet(er)i p(e)cc(at)ore? fiat iustus. ad tit(um). iii[..]
image-005 L6:  non ex op(er)ib(us) iusticie que fecim(us)
image-005 L7:  nos s(ed) s(e)c(un)d(u)m .s. m. s. n. f. p(er) lauacr[..]    [initials only, as written]
image-005 L8:  reg(e)n(erationis)?. et de. s. s. que(m) ef. in nos [..]
image-005 L9:  de. hec renouatio fit ad modum
image-005 L10: et ad similitudine(m) renouat(i)o(n)is      (= image-006 L1)
image-005 L11: c(er)ui qui cum antiq(ua)t(ur)? uult renou[..]   (= image-006 L2)
image-005 L12: at(tra)hit serpentem narib(us) et inue[..]   (= image-006 L3)
image-006 L4:  nat(us) currit ad fontem et biben[..]
image-006 L5:  purgat(ur). sic et nos antiq(ua)ti in p[..]
image-006 L6:  et inuenenati veneno p(ra)ue p(er)sua[..]
image-006 L7:  onis serpentis curramus ad fon[..]
image-006 L8:  bap(tism)i ut ibi purgemur et renoue[..]
image-006 L9:  In signu(m) hui(us) renouat(i)o(n)is dat(ur) [..]
image-006 L10: ero? vestis candida q(ua)m deferat? ant[..]
image-006 L11: t(ri)bunal iudicis. s(ed) homo it(er)um in[..]
image-006 L12: culatus? indiget s(e)c(un)da que est p[..]
image-006 L13: de tu(n)ica? lotium?/Jotime? iudas et sic(ut)? h[..]   (bottom line; middle words doubtful)

C. Marginalia on the first leaf (image-005/006, left margin) - not read:
"Fra:" (top left, later hand); cursive note beside L5-L9 beginning "+ bap..."? [illegible];
a 2-line note beside L10-L11 [illegible]; framed box with "7..."? "P..."? [illegible];
foot: "f? 49 ..."? [illegible].

4. LIMITATIONS
- A: every line has lost its opening letters; I leave the gap unfilled. L1 and L14 are the least
  secure. Red marks over words in L8, L9, L11, L13 may be deletions or just rubrication smears;
  I describe rather than interpret them.
- B: line ends are lost at the right edge (tab and page edge); gaps left open. In L7-L8 the scribe
  writes a quotation by initials only; I give the letters as seen.
- The relation of strip A to column B (same leaf? same text?) cannot be settled from the images.
  A flatter, wider shot of the first leaf's right edge and the next page would help.
